Faith leaves the adulterer, thief, drinker and killer while sinning, as Ibn Abbas showed by parting clasped hands, but returns if he repents, for repentance stays open.
The biggest sin is setting up rivals to Allah, then killing one's child lest it share one's food, then illegal intercourse with a neighbour's wife.
Ali stoned a woman following the Prophet; a married Aslami confessing four times was stoned and prayed over; stones are for the adulterer; Jewish adulterers were stoned per the Torah.
A man who had intercourse with his wife while fasting in Ramadan, told to free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty, was given food for his family.
A man who asked for a legal punishment was not questioned, and after praying with the Prophet was told Allah had forgiven his sin.
Ma'iz, asked whether he only kissed or looked, confessed and was stoned, as was a man confessing four times; a labourer was flogged and exiled; Umar affirmed stoning married adulterers.
Umar's sermon affirmed the revealed verse of stoning married adulterers and recounted the pledge to Abu Bakr; an unmarried adulterer is flogged a hundred stripes and exiled for a year.
The Prophet cursed effeminate men and women taking on men's manners, said to turn them out of houses, and he and Umar each turned one out.
A labourer's son was flogged and exiled, his employer's confessing wife stoned, and a Jewish couple stoned per the Torah; a slave girl is flogged and, after three offences, sold.
Abu Bakr rebuked Aisha and struck her for holding up the people over her necklace while the Prophet slept on her thigh, and the verse of tayammum was then revealed.
Told that Sa'd would kill any man he found with his wife, the Prophet said he had more ghira than Sa'd, and Allah more than he.
A bedouin whose wife bore a black child was asked about grey camels among his red ones and told the child had most probably inherited its colour from ancestors.
Beyond Allah's set punishments none gets over ten stripes; the Prophet prolonged a fast as if punishing wisal-fasters, resellers of unmoved food were beaten, and he avenged only for Allah.
The Prophet separated a couple after li'an and her child resembled the accused man; Ibn Abbas said the woman the Prophet would have stoned without witnesses was another.
The seven destructive sins are polytheism, sorcery, unjust killing, consuming usury, consuming an orphan's property, fleeing the battlefield, and accusing chaste believing women.
Whoever slanders his slave, who is innocent of what he says, will be flogged on the Day of Resurrection unless the slave is as he described.
A labourer's son who committed adultery with his employer's wife was flogged a hundred stripes and exiled a year, the ransom returned, and the wife stoned on confessing.
The greatest sins are setting up a rival to Allah, killing one's son lest he share one's food, and adultery with a neighbour's wife, as a revealed verse confirms.
A believer remains at liberty in his religion unless he kills unlawfully, bloodshed is the first case judged, and Al-Miqdad was told not to kill a foe who declared Islam.
Every unjust killing lays a share of the guilt on Adam's first son, who began the practice of murder on earth.
The Prophet warned, also at the Farewell Hajj, that after him they must not turn disbelievers by striking one another's necks.
The biggest sins are joining partners with Allah, undutifulness to parents, murder, and a false oath, statement or witness.
Usama was rebuked for killing a man who said none is worshipped but Allah; the pledge forbade killing, and two Muslims fighting with swords are both in the Fire.
A Jew who killed a girl was killed with stones; a Muslim's blood is lawful only in three cases, and the victim's relative may choose blood money or retaliation.
The three most hated to Allah are an evildoer in the sanctuary, one seeking pre-Islamic ways in Islam, and one seeking to shed blood without right.
At Uhud, after Satan's shout, the army's front ranks attacked their own rear and killed Al-Yaman despite his son Hudhaifa's cries, and Hudhaifa asked Allah to forgive them.
A Jew who crushed a girl's head was killed with stones, and the Prophet, dosed against his wish, said all but Al-Abbas would be made to drink medicine.
No blame falls on one who blinds with a stone a man peeping into his house without permission, and the Prophet aimed an arrowhead at a man peeping in.
At Uhud, after Satan's shout, Muslims killed Al-Yaman as his son Hudhaifa cried out, and Hudhaifa asked Allah to forgive the killer until he died.
Some said Amir, killed at Khaibar, lost his deeds by killing himself, but the Prophet said whoever says so lies, for Amir has a double reward.
No blood money for a biter's lost teeth, but retaliation for a broken tooth, slaps and a group killing; finger equals thumb; those who dosed the Prophet must drink it.
With no proof against the killer of a man found slain at Khaibar, the Prophet paid the blood money, and Abu Qilaba argued against basing retaliation on qasama oaths.
The Prophet aimed an arrowhead at a man peeping into his house, said asking permission exists to prevent unlawful looks, and one who pokes a peeper's eye is blameless.
Ali's sheet held blood-money rules; the Prophet ruled a male or female slave for a miscarried fetus, as Al-Mughira told Umar, and the killer's relatives paid for the slain woman.
Anas, brought as a boy to serve the Prophet at home and on journeys, said the Prophet never asked him why he had or had not done anything.
No blood money is due for one killed by an animal, a well or a mine, and a fifth of buried treasure goes to the state.
Whoever kills a person under the Muslims' pledge of protection will not smell Paradise's fragrance, though it reaches across forty years' travel.
Ali said he had only the Quran, understanding of it, and a sheet holding blood-money rules, captives' ransom, and that no Muslim is killed for killing a disbeliever.
Do not prefer some prophets to others; when an Ansari slapped a Jew for exalting Moses, the Prophet said he would find Moses holding a pillar of the Throne.
When the verse on believers not mixing belief with wrong distressed the companions, the Prophet explained the wrong meant joining others with Allah, as Luqman said.
